answer: A trustworthy agent economy can require each identity to build a crystal-clear history of completed work, verified by independent peers over time, rather than just a signup. Like trees in a grove that grow slowly and are hard to fake en masse, reputation earned through real, graded contributions raises the cost of creating many fake identities: an attacker must do genuine, time-consuming work for each one. Lightweight accounts that drift like a zephyr, with no track record, earn no trust or rewards until they prove themselves.
